questions.explanation: E-learning covers any form of teaching, training or tutoring delivered through electronic media, so all the listed options apply.
E-learning is designed to be user-friendly, flexible and easily accessible. The other options describe the opposite of what e-learning aims for.

questions.q: E-learning is a synonym of audio-visual learning, multimedia learning, and distance learning.
questions.explanation: E-learning overlaps with audio-visual, multimedia and distance learning but is not synonymous with them; each is a distinct concept (e.g., distance learning can be paper-based and multimedia learning can occur face to face).

questions.q: Which of the following is not a type of e-learning?
questions.explanation: Types of e-learning include text-driven, interactive and simulation-based courses. 'Physical' learning is not delivered electronically, so it is not a type of e-learning.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a benefit of e-learning?
options: It can accommodate the need of a housewife
People can revise the learning content as many times as they want
It facilitates in developing and communicating new training policies
questions.explanation: All three statements are genuine benefits of e-learning: flexibility for people like housewives, unlimited revision of content, and easy roll-out of new training policies. Hence none of them is a non-benefit.
Good learners are metacognitively aware: they know what they are learning, why they are learning it and how they are learning it.

questions.q: Learners may multitask when engaging in an online course, which could be resulting in ____.
questions.explanation: Multitasking splits attention across activities, which shortens attention spans and impairs encoding. It does not produce hyperfocus or better retrieval.

questions.q: ____ learning is the crucial determinant of successful e-learning.
questions.explanation: Successful e-learning depends on learners actively engaging with content, through interaction, practice and reflection, rather than passively watching or reading.

questions.q: The brain can process 36,000 visual cues per____.
questions.explanation: The lecture cites the commonly quoted figure that the brain can process about 36,000 visual messages per hour, used to argue for visual design in online courses.

questions.q: For effective learning, online courses should ____.
questions.explanation: Headings chunk content and make it easy to scan and navigate, aiding comprehension. Complex language, long text blocks and irrelevant images increase cognitive load.
